details:
USN-8927-1 fixed vulnerabilities in curl. This update provides the
corresponding fixes for Ubuntu 26.10.

Original advisory details:

 It was discovered that curl, when built with GnuTLS support, had an
 out-of-bounds read in the WebSocket send path. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information.
 (CVE-2026-107928)

 Maksim discovered that curl did not correctly include the interface
 binding in connection reuse decisions when CURLOPT_INTERFACE was used.
 An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause connections to go
 out from an unintended source address. (CVE-2026-107929)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that curl did not properly clear AWS SigV4
 authentication state when CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4 was set to NULL. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information.
 (CVE-2026-86409)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that the curl command line tool did not set
 SSH host verification options when following redirects to SFTP or SCP
 URLs. An attacker could possibly use this issue to perform
 machine-in-the-middle attacks. (CVE-2026-86410)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that curl did not properly handle cookie jar
 entries that could not be reloaded. An attacker could possibly use this
 issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-86412)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that an HTTP proxy could trick libcurl into
 sending credentials to the proxy itself by responding to a CONNECT
 request with an unexpected authentication challenge. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information.
 (CVE-2026-86414)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that curl did not correctly handle HSTS
 entries when an includeSubDomains parent entry was imported before a
 longer-lived child entry. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
 cause curl to use unencrypted HTTP connections. (CVE-2026-87862)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that curl did not properly handle HSTS
 max-age values that exceeded calendar time structure bounds. An
 attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or
 data loss. (CVE-2026-87863)

 Stanislav Fort discovered that curl did not properly handle IMAP APPEND
 commands when CURLOPT_CRLF was enabled, allowing overflow bytes to be
 interpreted as pipelined commands. An authenticated attacker could
 possibly use this issue to inject arbitrary IMAP commands.
 (CVE-2026-87864)

 Bobbeh Rhino discovered that libcurl, when used with libssh2 and a
 hashed known_hosts file, could misreport a host key mismatch as a
 missing key. An attacker could possibly use this issue to perform
 machine-in-the-middle attacks. (CVE-2026-87865)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that curl did not properly handle long cookie
 entries written to a Netscape cookie jar. An attacker could possibly
 use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-92386)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that a malicious FTP, IMAP, POP3, or SMTP
 server could cause libcurl to block indefinitely by omitting the final
 control-response line. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
 cause a denial of service. (CVE-2026-92387)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that libcurl had a use-after-free
 vulnerability in the FTP wildcard matching code. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause curl to crash, resulting in a denial
 of service, or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-92388)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that libcurl's TFTP state machine did not
 properly validate transfer directions, allowing a malicious server to
 force the client into transmit mode. An attacker could possibly use
 this issue to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-92389)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that curl did not properly enforce its file
 overwrite protection when using --remote-header-name in certain
 circumstances. An attacker could possibly use this issue to overwrite
 local files. (CVE-2026-92390)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that curl had a stack overflow vulnerability
 when processing deeply nested MIME structures. An attacker could
 possibly use this issue to cause curl to crash, resulting in a denial
 of service. (CVE-2026-92391)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that libcurl could expose credentials in the
 URL returned by CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL when credentials were retrieved
 from a .netrc file. An attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain
 sensitive information. (CVE-2026-94266)

 Joshua Rogers discovered that libcurl had a use-after-free
 vulnerability during HTTP/2 uploads when handling RST_STREAM responses
 from the server. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause
 curl to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary
 code. (CVE-2026-92392)
